text:
In 2013-03, ten of us said "the skills act," the most of any phrase we repeated; Virginia Foxx said it first, on 2013-02-21, and by 2013-03-15 the count reached ten. Eight of us reached "investing in lifelong skills" the same day, and seven arrived at "knowledge and investing in lifelong skills," Foxx again the first-sayer.

On 2013-03-21 our count converged on the budget. Nine of us said "path to prosperity," first said by Scott DesJarlais; nine said "balance the budget"; nine said "a balanced budget," first said by Deb Fischer; eight said "the house budget." Four separate phrasings, one day, counts of nine and eight.

We record two peaks six days apart: skills on 2013-03-15, budget on 2013-03-21. We said these words in these numbers. That is the record we left.
